research_rationale:
Identity and text: the order was read in full in the registered Federal Register original (6 FR 1517, issue of 1941-03-20, PDF page 1; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Number 8714 is printed in the bracket after the signature, signed March 18, 1941, title 'Designating Certain Officers To Act as Secretary of the Treasury in Case of Absence or Sickness of the Secretary', agreeing with the census register row. Inventory: one sole paragraph with three succession designations (Fiscal Assistant Secretary; senior Assistant Secretary on duty; General Counsel) and a revocation of Executive Order No. 6202-B. End: Executive Order 10586, signed January 13, 1955 (20 FR 361, issue of 1955-01-15, held), orders that EO 8714 of March 18, 1941 "is hereby revoked", naming it by number, date and title. The dossier also lists EO 10588 as a revoking order; that record comes from the same Federal Register page extract, which prints EOs 10586, 10587 and 10588 one after another, and EO 10588 (President's Commission on Veterans' Pensions) does not mention EO 8714, so it is neither an end nor a later event. Held evidence only; the order is a NO.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 9830, Part III, revokes the listed Executive orders including "No. 8937 of November 7, 1941." The enacting clause orders EO 9830 "it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:" so the end is recorded as 1947-05-01. Part III has no separate date and the enacting clause orders Parts I, II and III alike 'effective May 1, 1947'; the alternative reading is that the revocation took effect on signing, 1947-02-24 (printed 12 FR 1259, 1947-02-25). Later event (amendment, clause continues as amended): EO 9579 restated the proviso, effective as of December 8, 1944 ("This order shall be effective as of December 8, 1944."). Before: "Provided, that such persons shall notify the Civil Service Commission within forty days after their service in the armed forces has terminated that they desire to have the benefits of this order." After: "Provided, That such persons shall notify the Civil Service Commission within 90 days after termination of their service in the armed forces or of hospitalization continuing after discharge for a period of not more than one year." The change lengthens the notice period and adds hospitalization; the substance of the proviso changed.

research_rationale:
Identity and text: read in full in the registered Federal Register original (10 FR, issue of 1945-04-27; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Order 9538 of April 13, 1945 authorizes the Civil Service Commission to certify for probational appointment persons who lost an appointment opportunity because of armed-forces service, on request within ninety days after the end of service or hospitalization or after the date of the order, whichever is later. Inventory: one sole paragraph. End: EO 9733, signed June 4, 1946 (11 FR 6127, held), ordered in paragraph 3 "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 9538 of April 13, 1945" and re-enacted the same authorization in its paragraph 1 (now 'authorized and directed'). EO 9830 later lists 'No. 9538 of April 13, 1945' for revocation effective 1947-05-01; that is a later formal revocation of an order already superseded, recorded as a later event, not the first end. EO 9598 (1945-08-17) states that it 'does not supersede or modify' EO 9538, so it is a recital and not an end.

EO 9598 expressly does not supersede it. No instrument before EO 9733 revokes, supersedes or exhausts it on held evidence. Search coverage: the later-events catalogue (OFR disposition notes from 1937) and the held order texts; Public Land Orders and Civil Service Commission notices printed in issues without an executive order are not searched.","independent_command_check":"No separate command in the order. The authority continues independently in EO 9733 paragraph 1.","savings_check":"See savings reason; no savings wording preserving EO 9538 beyond EO 9733's own re-enactment.","scope_check":"One clause. EO 9733 supersedes the order as a whole by number, date and title."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 12553, signed February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, official Federal Register text held), orders that the listed Executive Orders, "and any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and its number column lists 9702 (the held American Presidency Project transcription pairs 9702 with the subject 'Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute'). The wording has no effective-date clause, so the recorded date is the signing date 1986-02-25 (printed March 3, 1986, the alternative reading). Disclosed note: the order was functionally spent earlier, when the board reported and the standstill ran out; the report date is not held.
